evidence: Old Player.tscn imports Models/FPSPlayer.glb and authored Climbing, ClimbingSide, Mantle, Fist/Knife/OneHand/Wand, FistThrow, KickParrySpecial and KickPushAttack animations.
Old Player.gd implements five-step combo state, timed hitboxes/transitions, stamina, hold block, early parry window, attack interruption and post-attack movement slowdown.
Fist state machine includes five-hit chain, sprint attack, blocking and a parry transition into KickPushAttack.

Drew remembers Generation 1 as the tunnel-maze Infinite Brutality, Generation 2 as the climbing version, with the climbing capability and FPS arm lineage inherited into modern Infinite Brutality. Old arms originally had metal bracers later removed for a less-fantasy read.
Modern project identifies assets/models/FPSPlayer.glb as its first-person arm/animation source copied from Pose Lab and documents live climbing/mantle traversal machinery.

Drew states the old InfiniteBrutality work, including the procedural Minecraft-like voxel-world effort, was completely his work with no AI assistance. He identifies it as a uniquely important pre-AI specimen of how he independently thinks and reasons, useful as a baseline against later AI-assisted collaboration.

Drew identifies the old solo-authored procedural floating/voxel world lineage as the stronger public taste-drop direction and rejects Boxcraft as the consumer-facing fantasy. Boxcraft may remain useful internal deterministic traversal grammar, but the player-facing artifact should expose explorable spatial possibility rather than box-generation machinery.
